subject: Post-demo: FinOpt performance targets & connection strategy
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kai Lopez <kai.lopez@finopt.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: FinOpt performance targets & connection strategy

Hi Kai — thanks again for the time today, really appreciated the deep dive from your engineering team. Quick recap and three asks so we can size a pilot and proposal: 

Recap (from demo)
- Primary use: realtime assistant for underwriters (short prompts, streaming updates to UI)
- Target latency: 95th pctl end-to-end <= 200 ms for non-streaming generation; for streaming, per-chunk latency target ~70 ms
- Expected payloads: median request ~120 tokens, peak bursts up to ~2k tokens for long explanations
- Traffic profile: steady-state 350 qps, expected sustained concurrency ~600 parallel requests, peak concurrency ~1,800 during batch processing windows

Three asks for us to finalize a pilot plan: 
1) Confirm the concurrency numbers above (steady / sustained / peak) and whether streaming will be used for >50% of flows. 
2) Share any hard SLOs (p95, p99) that would require an SLA. 
3) Any procurement/PO timing constraints and the preferred runway for a 6-week pilot.

Attachments: finopt-performance-sheet.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB) — I dropped a simple table with token and concurrency assumptions. Also putting the demo recording in Drive: https://drive.google.com/finopt-poc-plan

Next steps: if you confirm concurrency and streaming % by EOD Friday, we can turn around a pilot capacity plan (routing + connection pooling + rate caps) and a draft canary schedule.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0137

From: Kai Lopez <kai.lopez@finopt.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinOpt performance targets & connection strategy

Jordan — thanks for the recap and the sheet, that's helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Concurrency: your numbers are close. Our production estimate is steady 300 qps, sustained concurrency ~550, but we're planning a couple of scheduled heavy windows (ET close/batch runs) that will push to ~1,600 for short periods (10-15 minutes).
- Streaming: yes, we plan to use streaming for the assistant UI for ~65% of interactions. Per-chunk sizes will be small (~25-50 tokens) but frequent.
- SLOs: p95 token latency target: <= 180 ms non-streaming; streaming per-chunk p95 <= 60 ms. We can be flexible on p99 for pilot but want p95 guarantees.

Procurement: target to sign a pilot PO in 3 weeks. We're open to a credit-based pilot or committed capacity for the pilot — flexibility appreciated.

Questions for Redwood: what are typical per-API-key rate limits, and how does connection pooling interact with per-token RPS? Also curious about burst windows (you mentioned token buckets) and whether we can get a temporary increase for the heavy windows.

Appreciate the quick follow-up — Kai
Kai Lopez
Head of Platform Engineering | FinOpt
kai.lopez@finopt.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: FinOpt performance targets & connection strategy (internal)

Jordan / Marissa — forwarding Kai's reply. High-level options we should propose back (technical + commercial):

1) Hosted pilot (fastest)
   - Baseline rate cap: 500 RPS per project key (enough for 300 steady qps with connection pooling);
   - Burst window: token-bucket configured for 2,000 RPS equivalent for up to 10 minutes (guarded by burst credits);
   - Connection pooling: recommend long-lived websockets with multiplexing (each socket can carry multiple parallel requests). We should document recommended SDK settings (max_inflight=200 per socket, keepalive=60s).

2) Dedicated pool (if they need strict p95 SLA)
   - Dedicated GPU pool with reserved throughput ~2x sustained expected qps (target 1,200 sustained capacity) so p95 headroom for peaks;
   - Predictable latency SLA (p95 <= 150 ms) and capacity-based billing;

3) Short-term hybrid: start with hosted pilot + temporary burst increases for their ET windows (manual escalation policy + credits).

Pricing/credits note: for pilot we can offer $Xk in usage credits if they commit to a sales-qualified PO within 3 weeks. Also suggest a simple canary plan: week 1 small traffic, week 2 ramp 10x, week 3 full traffic on hosted with monitoring, week 4 optional move to dedicated if p95/SLA required.

Action items for us:
- Jordan: deliver a clear table mapping their concurrency numbers to recommended config (baseline rate caps, sockets, burst buckets).
- Marissa: draft the pilot commercial (credits + PO language) and DocuSign link.

I'll loop infra if we need a temporary quota bump.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kai Lopez <kai.lopez@finopt.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinOpt performance targets & connection strategy

Kai — appreciate the quick clarifications. Based on your numbers and Grace's notes, here's a proposed pilot package we can turn around immediately: 

Pilot proposal (6 weeks)
- Hosted pilot with temporary burst allowances
  - Baseline rate limits: 500 RPS per project API key (recommended for your steady-state 300 qps)
  - Sustained concurrency guidance: connection pooling with websockets, max_inflight=200 per socket yields ~250 parallel requests per socket; recommend 3-4 sockets per service instance
  - Burst window: allow up to 2,000 RPS equivalent for up to 12 minutes, enforced by token-bucket; this is designed to absorb the 1,600 peaks you described without immediate throttling
  - Streaming: optimized fast-path for small per-chunk responses (Grace will supply SDK tune parameters). Target streaming p95<=60 ms with these settings (pilot only).

- Optional Dedicated upgrade (post-pilot)
  - Reserved pool configured for 1,200 sustained throughput to give headroom for p95 SLA <=150 ms
  - Predictable capacity-based billing and SLA addendum (if required).

Commercials & next steps
- Pilot credits: we can offer a $25k usage credit for the pilot tied to a short PO (3-week sign window).
- DocuSign: Marissa will send a simple SOW and PO link (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/678901 / https://na1.docusign.net/finopt-pilot)
- Monitoring: we will provision a shared dashboard and a token-level cost/latency view; add your SREs as viewers.

If you confirm (A) acceptance of pilot config above and (B) preferred PO sign-by date, we'll lock in a start date and can schedule an infra quota bump for your first heavy window.

Attachment: finopt-performance-sheet.xlsx (see tab "Pilot Assumptions")

Thanks and happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk the config.

— Jordan
